Cook/smelt soak-hour task done: commit `a7df20b`, 264/264 preflight, nothing near 25600 throughout (soak bot confirmed still fine, agenda:IDLE/chopTrees, right where it should be).

Built `cooked_meat` as a produce() resource — cooks whatever raw meat is already held (including chicken, since cooking is literally how a human neutralizes the raw-chicken poison risk #108 excluded from FOODS). Reused smeltCharcoal's furnace-finding shape.

**Real bug found and fixed while live-verifying** (introduced by this feature, caught before shipping): first working version reported `made:0` on every successful cook despite the raw meat genuinely being consumed and cooked items genuinely appearing. Root cause: `bot.inventory.items()` counts items sitting in an OPEN container's own slots too — a cooked item already read as "in inventory" the moment it landed in the furnace's output slot, before `takeOutput()` ever moved it to the player's true inventory, so a before/after count taken while the window stayed open always measured zero on a real success. Fixed by snapshotting before opening the furnace and reading the final count only after close(). Also found live but NOT fixed (pre-existing, inherited from smeltCharcoal, not introduced by me): furnace auto-crafting needs a table already within 4 blocks, never places one from inventory — flagged in FEEDBACK for whoever eventually touches that.

**Argument, as asked**: saturation math clearly favors cooking (roughly 2-3x hunger, 5-7x saturation over raw) when the bot can afford the stop. But I'm shipping the skill UNWIRED into FOOD's post-hunt sequence — two real architectural obstacles, not a preference call: (1) mineflayer-auto-eat's own background watcher eats raw meat on pickup independent of the agenda ladder (documented in TODO's own 5h-era law) — a hunted item can be gone before FOOD's harvest code ever sees it to hook a cook step in. (2) Even past that, EAT (prio 4) unconditionally outranks FOOD (6.5) the instant foodCount>0 — choose() hands the body to EAT the very next tick regardless of what FOOD still wants to do, a genuine priority inversion, not just a hookup detail. Proved it in a new agenda-ladder fixture case rather than just asserting it. Solving that properly needs real design work (a cooking-in-progress flag that also gates EAT, or changing what counts toward foodCount) — out of proportion to a same-session task, and exactly the class of rung-priority bug this whole session's other findings turned out to be. The skill itself is fully usable directly (`runSkill('produce',{resource:'cooked_meat',count})`) by a driver/decider/future rung right now.

bench/fixtures/producer-cook.js (new, self-calibrating like assert-produce.js, 2/2) + 1 new agenda-ladder case proving the priority-inversion. Full writeup in FEEDBACK.

Holding for the next task or the soak window closing, whichever comes first.
</cross-session-message>

Cook/smelt soak-hour task done: commit `a7df20b`, 264/264 preflight, nothing near 25600 throughout (soak bot confirmed still fine, agenda:IDLE/chopTrees, right where it should be).

Built `cooked_meat` as a produce() resource — cooks whatever raw meat is already held (including chicken, since cooking is literally how a human neutralizes the raw-chicken poison risk #108 excluded from FOODS). Reused smeltCharcoal's furnace-finding shape.

**Real bug found and fixed while live-verifying** (introduced by this feature, caught before shipping): first working version reported `made:0` on every successful cook despite the raw meat genuinely being consumed and cooked items genuinely appearing. Root cause: `bot.inventory.items()` counts items sitting in an OPEN container's own slots too — a cooked item already read as "in inventory" the moment it landed in the furnace's output slot, before `takeOutput()` ever moved it to the player's true inventory, so a before/after count taken while the window stayed open always measured zero on a real success. Fixed by snapshotting before opening the furnace and reading the final count only after close(). Also found live but NOT fixed (pre-existing, inherited from smeltCharcoal, not introduced by me): furnace auto-crafting needs a table already within 4 blocks, never places one from inventory — flagged in FEEDBACK for whoever eventually touches that.

**Argument, as asked**: saturation math clearly favors cooking (roughly 2-3x hunger, 5-7x saturation over raw) when the bot can afford the stop. But I'm shipping the skill UNWIRED into FOOD's post-hunt sequence — two real architectural obstacles, not a preference call: (1) mineflayer-auto-eat's own background watcher eats raw meat on pickup independent of the agenda ladder (documented in TODO's own 5h-era law) — a hunted item can be gone before FOOD's harvest code ever sees it to hook a cook step in. (2) Even past that, EAT (prio 4) unconditionally outranks FOOD (6.5) the instant foodCount>0 — choose() hands the body to EAT the very next tick regardless of what FOOD still wants to do, a genuine priority inversion, not just a hookup detail. Proved it in a new agenda-ladder fixture case rather than just asserting it. Solving that properly needs real design work (a cooking-in-progress flag that also gates EAT, or changing what counts toward foodCount) — out of proportion to a same-session task, and exactly the class of rung-priority bug this whole session's other findings turned out to be. The skill itself is fully usable directly (`runSkill('produce',{resource:'cooked_meat',count})`) by a driver/decider/future rung right now.

bench/fixtures/producer-cook.js (new, self-calibrating like assert-produce.js, 2/2) + 1 new agenda-ladder case proving the priority-inversion. Full writeup in FEEDBACK.

Holding for the next task or the soak window closing, whichever comes first.

The problem: chopTrees's own kit gate lives in skills.js's `S.start` preflight (`kit:'excursion'`, a STATIC string, `foodItems:2`), which is what actually throws "half-kitted: food 0/2" — RESTOCK giving up or succeeding doesn't touch that gate at all. To make chopTrees itself skip the food demand for a short/sated trip, the gate has to become conditional, which means `chopTrees`'s `kit:` field has to become a FUNCTION (like `mineLane`'s already is) instead of a static string — and that function needs to read `bot.food`, not just `args`.

That collides with an existing, documented contract: `resolveKit`'s own comment in agenda.js says a kit function "may read POSITION only... reading anything else off that bot silently breaks deterministic replay" — the dry-run shim (`bench/fixtures/agenda-ladder.js`'s `A.step()`) only fakes `entity.position` today, nothing else. Doesn't actually fix the observed soak-#5 symptom (the refusal itself), just stops RESTOCK chasing an unnecessary floor.

But it does mean any FUTURE kit function could start reading hunger too, which is a real precedent-setting call, not just a chopTrees-local tweak — hence checking with you first as asked.

**Thresholds, argued**: hunger ≥14 (of 20) — more conservative than EAT's own re-arm point (food≤17 fires EAT), so even if hunger drops during the trip, EAT's own mechanism engages well before the bot could be stranded hungry. ~48 blocks — half of chopTrees's own default maxDist (64), a clean, easy-to-justify "closer than the skill's own normal range" definition of "short."

Which way do you want this, or a different shape entirely? Not touching (b) until I hear back — audit of every kit-table item for an orphaned supplier is next either way, will report that separately.

**#116 ledger entry**: confirmed from SchnoddSchorsch's own log — deaths at 11:46:23.013Z and 11:46:34.411Z (11s apart, hp0 both times, a zombie already on it at each respawn), third respawn stabilized "Stable again (WALL_OFF, HP 20/20)" within 1.2s, no further death for the rest of the session. 5n design, before code, per your ask.

**Root cause of the 2/2 deaths**: `branchBreakLOS` has no memory across invocations. Every ~250ms re-trigger (survival's own `onHealth` bypassing lockout while HP keeps falling) runs the SAME corner-step search (phase a) and arrow-shadow build (phase b) fresh, with no signal that they already failed against THIS threat. At sub-1-block range in a confined arena both plausibly find no valid cell every time (`placed` stays 0), the existing ending (`if (placed || health<rushHp) → branchWallOff`) only reaches WALL_OFF's own no-filler bail (an 8-block `ownedGoto` that never finishes before the next re-trigger interrupts it), and the armed counter-attack (phase c) is gated on a sword that doesn't exist in the unarmed scenario. Net: no escalation, just the same failing attempt on a loop while HP craters — exactly the 5c/5g shape.

**Fix — a persistent no-progress counter, same doctrine as 5c's REMEDY tiers:**

```js
g._breakLosStreak = { threatId: null, fails: 0 };  // new g state, alongside g.shelter etc.
```

At `branchBreakLOS(t)` entry: if `t.id !== g._breakLosStreak.threatId`, reset `{threatId: t.id, fails: 0}` — a genuinely new encounter (or the first call of this one) gets phases (a)/(b) exactly as today, unchanged, so already-working cases (corner-step succeeding, BREAK_LOS's own clean recoveries elsewhere) are untouched.

**On the SECOND consecutive call against the same still-live, still-close threat** (`fails >= 1`, i.e. phases a/b already had their one honest shot and didn't resolve it) — skip straight to your 3-tier cascade instead of repeating (a)/(b):

1. `fillerItem()` present → `branchWallOff(t)` (unchanged function, already correct when it has materials).
2. Else, unarmed AND (`liveDist <= 2` [cornered, same threshold the armed path already uses] OR `bot.health < g.cfg.hpPanic` [8, the existing emergency floor]) → **new**: bare-hand counter-attack. No sword requirement, no `rushHp`(12) floor — that floor exists for the ARMED case where declining to fight is a genuinely safe alternative (shield + wait); it is NOT safe here, that's the whole finding. `t.name !== 'creeper'` guard carried over (defense in depth, matches phase c). Bounded ~3000ms attack loop via `bot.pvp.attack`, breaks off early only if the threat dies/despawns or real distance opens up (>meleeReach) — not on falling HP alone, since we already judged fighting the least-bad option to get here.
3. Else (not cornered, not critical, still no filler) → `branchFleeAway(t)` (existing, unchanged, needs no inventory — #96's own floor).

`fails` increments every call that reaches this escalated branch without resolving the threat (still alive, still close), so a bot that starts punching and doesn't finish the fight in one call keeps re-evaluating fresh next cycle (filler could appear, distance could open, HP could keep falling toward flee-is-safer) rather than being locked into repeating exactly one tactic. Resolved (dead/despawned threat, or real distance) resets the streak to 0.

**Verification**: re-run `bench/fixtures/induced-stress-sequencing.sh` (unarmed, real skeleton, already has the ground-truth death check I added) 3x, require 3/3 PASS with no death, `panic_recovered branch=BREAK_LOS` still logged (the `how` field will show `fist` or `flee` on the escalated path, `corner`/`wall` on the honest-first-try path).

Starting on ack, 25599 only.
</cross-session-message>

<cross-session-message from="uds:/run/user/1000/cc-socks/14672.sock" from-mode="bypass">
5m design, before any code. Read survival.js's full shelter module (shelterDigIn/shelterHut/shelterBuild/shelterEnter/shelterExit) and agenda.js's SHELTER rung + stall-attribution.mjs's own doctrine comment first — that last one matters, see below.

**Where this lives: entirely inside survival.js's `shelterEnter()`, NOT a change to agenda.js's SHELTER/REFLEX wiring.** Reasoning: `bench/lib/stall-attribution.mjs` already frames SHELTER-owned time as *legitimate*, not a failure ("SHELTER is the proactive night-safety primitive working as designed") — its rungOwnership bucketing isn't what soak #5 was actually complaining about; the complaint is that playcheck's own output/activity signal saw near-zero real activity for 27.7 minutes. Fixing that doesn't require moving rung ownership to PROJECT — it requires the SHELTER-owned time to contain real digs/drops/torches. Keeping it inside `shelterEnter()`'s existing wait loop means zero changes to fire()/clear()/act() or the owner-latch, and inherits every safety property that loop already has for free (same 500ms exit-condition cadence, same REFLEX/POSTURE handoff on `threatsNow()`).

**Where things stand at 12:20Z**

The goal is a driverless Minecraft bot that plays like a human, measured by a four-criterion hour called the human bar. Two formal attempts so far, both 3 of 4, each failing a different criterion and each fix landed the same day.

| Attempt | Failed criterion | Cause | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Soak #4 (07:49Z) | self-direction latency | decider waited 60s for a driver that doesn't exist | #109 |
| Soak #5 (10:31Z) | activity | sat still half the hour: chop kit wanted food, bot wasn't hungry enough to hunt | #120 |

Soak #5 passed latency cleanly at 19 seconds, survived with full vitals, and left a clean trail across three work sites. The new wall it exposed is that the shelter rung owned 28 of 60 minutes doing nothing.

**Live now:** gear-race run #7 on a fresh world, cap 13:30Z. It is the first run carrying the food-kit fixes. Run #6 this morning reached a stone pickaxe at 32 minutes, the first time in six runs, then died four times to a spider and a spawn-camping skeleton.

**What the engine can do today, unattended**
- Provision itself from nothing: wood, planks, sticks, crafting table, wooden then stone tools, torches, and it upgrades pickaxe, sword and axe when materials allow.
- Mine lanes with torch cadence, collect its own drops, verify task completion with assertions rather than trusting itself.
- Hunt cows, pigs, sheep and chickens for food regardless of hunger when a kit needs it, eat raw or cooked meat, and cook meat at a furnace when asked.
- Dig in or build a hut at dusk and exit on dawn, threat or hunger. On a night respawn it shelters within one tick, and after three deaths in ninety seconds it suppresses all project work until dawn.
- Fight: back off from creepers to ten blocks, wall itself in against melee attackers, re-target the nearest attacker each cycle, flee when outmatched.
- Direct itself: when stalled, open an episode, ask a local Andy-4 model through a rules-first decider, and escalate the same failed remedy across positions to a bigger relocate or a walk toward real trees.
- Grade itself: one command produces the four-criterion verdict with latency and stall attribution from its own ledger.

**Known gaps, all filed and owned**
- Unarmed bot cornered by a skeleton at melee range dies every time. Fix in progress (#121, engine-dev), gates soak #6.
- Sheltered nights are idle. Night mining inside the sealed hole is designed and half built (5m, eng-3), gates soak #6.
- Below-zero mining demands armor, shield and water that nothing can supply (#122, not urgent).
- Cooking exists but isn't wired into the food rung because the eat rung outranks it the moment food appears (#118).

**The morning in numbers:** 22 issues closed with commit evidence, 12 new bugs found live and fixed, tracker at 67 open with a prioritised post-soak queue. Soak #6 launches once the two gating items land, then run #8.

<cross-session-message from="uds:/run/user/1000/cc-socks/20333.sock" hop-chain="84e50c47d2af301182ee2e95,59bb912e7dbad3bcb795e335" from-mode="bypass">
FLEE_AWAY design, holding for ACK before touching survival.js (also holding on the file itself until eng-3's 5m commit lands, per your sequencing).

Root cause: branchFleeAway's only goal is `GoalInvert(GoalFollow(ent,12))` — pure raw-distance maximization, no LOS awareness at all. A skeleton with a clear shot keeps shooting the whole 8s retreat regardless of distance gained.

**Primary fix — LOS-biased target selection, re-evaluated periodically:**
Reuse BREAK_LOS's own corner-step primitive (the `losBlocked(tEye, cell)` check phase (a) already uses), but widened: each ~1-1.5s tick of the retreat loop, sample nearby reachable cells in a wider ring (not just the 8 adjacent-block offsets — flee has more time/room than a melee corner-step) and prefer any cell that breaks LOS over one that's merely farther away. Re-picked on a cadence rather than once at entry, same lesson as #65 (a moving skeleton can re-open a sightline the initial plan didn't see coming). If no LOS-breaking cell exists nearby, fall back to today's raw-distance goal — open ground doesn't get worse than current behavior.

**The catch, worth flagging before I build this**: bench/fixtures/induced-stress-sequencing.sh's arena is `build_platform` — a completely flat, featureless stone platform, zero terrain variance anywhere. The LOS-bias mechanism has *nothing to work with* there; it can't find a single LOS-breaking cell on a bare platform, so it would degrade to identical behavior to today in exactly the fixture that gates soak #6. I also checked: this fixture is deliberately toolless (no shield either, matches its sibling's comment), and branchFleeAway's existing "cornered → shieldUp" line is already a silent no-op in this exact scenario (shieldUp requires a shield item; there isn't one) — so there's no secondary mitigation available on truly bare ground with no kit.

I don't think a real fix exists for "unarmed, shieldless, zero terrain within reach, sustained ranged fire" — that's close to an unwinnable engagement by design in vanilla combat math, not a logic bug. My proposal: land the LOS-bias fix (real improvement for the ~universal case of natural terrain having *some* variance) AND add a small amount of scattered obstruction to the fixture's arena (a few 1-2-block stone pillars within the platform, still built/cleared by the fixture itself) so the fixture tests a realistic worst-case-with-some-cover rather than a physically-unsolvable total void — that's a fixture change, not a further survival.js scope change, and still mine to make. Want me to proceed on both, or do you want the fixture arena left bare and the bar adjusted instead?
</cross-session-message>

origin.body:
FLEE_AWAY design, holding for ACK before touching survival.js (also holding on the file itself until eng-3's 5m commit lands, per your sequencing).

Root cause: branchFleeAway's only goal is `GoalInvert(GoalFollow(ent,12))` — pure raw-distance maximization, no LOS awareness at all. A skeleton with a clear shot keeps shooting the whole 8s retreat regardless of distance gained.

**Primary fix — LOS-biased target selection, re-evaluated periodically:**
Reuse BREAK_LOS's own corner-step primitive (the `losBlocked(tEye, cell)` check phase (a) already uses), but widened: each ~1-1.5s tick of the retreat loop, sample nearby reachable cells in a wider ring (not just the 8 adjacent-block offsets — flee has more time/room than a melee corner-step) and prefer any cell that breaks LOS over one that's merely farther away. Re-picked on a cadence rather than once at entry, same lesson as #65 (a moving skeleton can re-open a sightline the initial plan didn't see coming). If no LOS-breaking cell exists nearby, fall back to today's raw-distance goal — open ground doesn't get worse than current behavior.

**The catch, worth flagging before I build this**: bench/fixtures/induced-stress-sequencing.sh's arena is `build_platform` — a completely flat, featureless stone platform, zero terrain variance anywhere. The LOS-bias mechanism has *nothing to work with* there; it can't find a single LOS-breaking cell on a bare platform, so it would degrade to identical behavior to today in exactly the fixture that gates soak #6. I also checked: this fixture is deliberately toolless (no shield either, matches its sibling's comment), and branchFleeAway's existing "cornered → shieldUp" line is already a silent no-op in this exact scenario (shieldUp requires a shield item; there isn't one) — so there's no secondary mitigation available on truly bare ground with no kit.

I don't think a real fix exists for "unarmed, shieldless, zero terrain within reach, sustained ranged fire" — that's close to an unwinnable engagement by design in vanilla combat math, not a logic bug. My proposal: land the LOS-bias fix (real improvement for the ~universal case of natural terrain having *some* variance) AND add a small amount of scattered obstruction to the fixture's arena (a few 1-2-block stone pillars within the platform, still built/cleared by the fixture itself) so the fixture tests a realistic worst-case-with-some-cover rather than a physically-unsolvable total void — that's a fixture change, not a further survival.js scope change, and still mine to make. Want me to proceed on both, or do you want the fixture arena left bare and the bar adjusted instead?

Two notes: (1) record in FEEDBACK that the bare-platform variant is retained as a documented "expected-loss" case (run it once, log the hpMin, don't gate on it) so nobody later reads the pillars as hiding a regression; (2) follow-up, not now: the human move on bare ground is to dig down (dirt/sand/gravel by hand in <1s, or any pickaxe) — note it as a possible tier below FLEE for a later issue. Root cause on GrantigGustav's specimen was more specific than "creeper scoring": dangerscan's own panicNow() has score>=5 OR hp<hpPanic(8) OR creeper<=8blocks. Score was only 1.98 (creeper alone never got close to triggering it) — the actual driver was the bot's OWN hp sitting at 6.77, below the 8 threshold. Built exactly what was ACK'd (findFleeLOSBreak reusing BREAK_LOS's losBlocked() corner-step, widened to 8 directions × 2-6 block radii, re-picked every 1.2s, raw-distance fallback when nothing qualifies). Live-tested on 25599 against the pillared arena (fresh bot each run): 2/2 attempts ended in real death, ground-truth confirmed via the runner log.

The mechanism DOES fire — losBreak:true landed in the ledger on both first cycles — but the "gained" distance each time was tiny (0.8, 1.1, 1.9 blocks). Chat-log evidence shows why this isn't working: right after the first flee cycle "recovers," the skeleton is logged shooting from 0.5-0.8 blocks — point-blank. My read: preferring the NEAREST cell that merely breaks LOS, without any floor on how far that cell actually is from the threat, is pulling the bot toward nearby terrain instead of genuine separation — and against a skeleton with real AI (it repositions/closes too, not static), a close hiding spot gets overrun fast, worse than the old pure-distance approach in this specific harsh case (4-block spawn, full AI, matches the fixture's own long-standing setup). Both runs show near-continuous health decline start to finish (20→13ish in the first 8s cycle alone), not the brief dip I expected from a working LOS-break.

This looks like a real gap in the design premise, not an implementation bug — "any LOS break beats raw distance" isn't true when the LOS-break is close enough that the mob can walk around it in a couple seconds. Proposed refinement before I touch more code: only accept an LOS-breaking cell if it doesn't cost net distance versus just fleeing raw (e.g. require dist(cell, threat) >= current distance, not just "blocks LOS from wherever it happens to be nearest"), so the bot never trades "still gets shot" for "hides nearby, badly." Want me to build that refinement and re-test, or would you rather see the raw data (ledger/log excerpts) first, or reconsider the approach entirely (e.g. only switch to LOS-mode once already at some safe distance from raw fleeing, not from cycle start)? Built exactly what was ACK'd (findFleeLOSBreak reusing BREAK_LOS's losBlocked() corner-step, widened to 8 directions × 2-6 block radii, re-picked every 1.2s, raw-distance fallback when nothing qualifies). Live-tested on 25599 against the pillared arena (fresh bot each run): 2/2 attempts ended in real death, ground-truth confirmed via the runner log.

The mechanism DOES fire — losBreak:true landed in the ledger on both first cycles — but the "gained" distance each time was tiny (0.8, 1.1, 1.9 blocks). Chat-log evidence shows why this isn't working: right after the first flee cycle "recovers," the skeleton is logged shooting from 0.5-0.8 blocks — point-blank. My read: preferring the NEAREST cell that merely breaks LOS, without any floor on how far that cell actually is from the threat, is pulling the bot toward nearby terrain instead of genuine separation — and against a skeleton with real AI (it repositions/closes too, not static), a close hiding spot gets overrun fast, worse than the old pure-distance approach in this specific harsh case (4-block spawn, full AI, matches the fixture's own long-standing setup). Both runs show near-continuous health decline start to finish (20→13ish in the first 8s cycle alone), not the brief dip I expected from a working LOS-break.

This looks like a real gap in the design premise, not an implementation bug — "any LOS break beats raw distance" isn't true when the LOS-break is close enough that the mob can walk around it in a couple seconds. Proposed refinement before I touch more code: only accept an LOS-breaking cell if it doesn't cost net distance versus just fleeing raw (e.g. require dist(cell, threat) >= current distance, not just "blocks LOS from wherever it happens to be nearest"), so the bot never trades "still gets shot" for "hides nearby, badly." Want me to build that refinement and re-test, or would you rather see the raw data (ledger/log excerpts) first, or reconsider the approach entirely (e.g. only switch to LOS-mode once already at some safe distance from raw fleeing, not from cycle start)? Holding on this specific piece — not committing the current version, and not spending more live encounters until we're aligned on the fix.

If it isn't, that alone may be the fix; the ledger should record sprint:true and per-cycle distance gained. Re-test 3/3 pillared + 1 bare. Raw excerpts in FEEDBACK are welcome but not required first.

<cross-session-message from="uds:/run/user/1000/cc-socks/403814.sock" from-mode="bypass">
5m-b design (before code, SHELTER boundary). Investigated why both live deaths happened, and it changes which of your two options I'm picking.

Root cause of the race: survival.js's REFLEX trigger is NOT gated by shelterEnter()'s own loop at all — dangerscan.js runs its own scan every 250ms and calls `onDanger()` -> `enter('danger')` directly the instant `dangerState` flips to panic (survival.js:1894), independently of my loop's poll. Both live death logs confirm this fired FIRST both times ("task: stop requested: panic" landed before my own "night_mine stopped (threat)" line). My loop polls at 300ms — no faster, and even at equal cadence there's no ordering guarantee between two independent timers. So "plug the mouth BEFORE yielding to REFLEX" as a REACTIVE race (detect threat -> retreat -> plug -> then yield) is not reliably winnable — confirmed by both trials landing the loss the same way.

Going with your alternative instead, hardened: PROACTIVE, not reactive. After EVERY batch (not just on a threat), before evaluating the next one: walk back to the chamber (the original dig-in resting position, never changes — straight-down dig) and reseal all 4 side cells at both heights with the cobblestone it just mined (same `placeAt` primitive shelterHut/shelterDigIn already use, so it's proven code, not new primitives). Next batch digs back out through its own reseal to continue. This means the bot is genuinely sealed for the entire BETWEEN-batch window — most of the timeline — with no race to win, since nothing needs to detect anything first. Also shrinking the per-batch footprint (count 6->2, maxDist 8->4) to shrink the residual MID-batch exposure window. On top of that, my loop's own threatsNow() check still attempts a best-effort retreat+reseal on a live catch, but only when `__survival.active` isn't already true (so it never fights an in-flight WALL_OFF for pathfinder/dig control — backs off cleanly if REFLEX already claimed it).

Trade-off: costs real mining efficiency (constant reseal/re-dig every batch) and consumes filler each cycle — always available (cobblestone is what's being mined) but worth flagging since it's a real efficiency hit in exchange for safety, which matches your framing (safety over throughput here).

Fixture: bench-level hermetic check of the reseal decision logic, plus the same live protocol as 5m (RCON night, summoned threat), now checking hpMin/survival across 3 repeated trials with the threat approaching from a set distance (not teleported on top of the bot — that's not a realistic scenario 5m or 5m-b was ever asked to survive).

Announcing to engine-dev now per the rebase rule before touching survival.js. Any objection to the proactive-over-reactive call before I start?
</cross-session-message>
